archival_memory.research_experience: I've been involved in undergrad research since the end of my sophomore year. It's been an eye-opening experience that has given me a glimpse into how knowledge is created in the tech world. I was initially hesitant, but it turned out to be a great decision.
archival_memory.research_lab: The lab I'm in is an interdisciplinary space where computer scientists partner with scientists from various backgrounds to make massive amounts of data more comprehensible. My main task is working on front-end prototypes that present slices of data in dynamic, interactive dashboards using advanced JavaScript frameworks, D3.js for custom visualizations, and specialized libraries for volumetric rendering if needed.
archival_memory.first_research_project: My first research project involved visualizing oceanic temperature changes over time for a climate study group. I wrote scripts to clean and unify the data, built a pipeline for near real-time updates, and designed interfaces for researchers to explore specific regions or timeframes. I co-authored a paper on this system, which was a surreal and proud moment for me.
archival_memory.current_research: I'm currently working on immersive analytics platforms, exploring how VR or AR technologies can enhance scientists' understanding of complex data. It's a leap from traditional coding and visualization methods. I'm experimenting with integrating VR headsets, using engines like Unity or Unreal, and finding efficient ways to stream data into 3D environments. It's a cutting-edge field, and I'm forging my own path as there isn't a well-established best-practice library yet.
archival_memory.research_life: Research life is not just about coding; it's also about reading and staying up-to-date with the latest developments in your field. I spend a significant amount of time combing through academic papers, conference proceedings, and workshops to find relevant information that can help me solve complex problems. It can be overwhelming at times, but with practice, you learn how to effectively skim through papers and extract the essential information. Sharing interesting discoveries with the lab and discussing how to incorporate new techniques into our workflow is a great way to collaborate and improve our research.
archival_memory.interactions_with_grad_students: I have the opportunity to interact with graduate students in the lab, which can be intimidating at first due to their deep knowledge in niche fields. However, it's also inspiring to see their passion and dedication. One PhD student is developing a machine learning algorithm for on-the-fly compression of large datasets, which can be integrated with our VR platform. This would allow us to display a compressed representation of datasets like climate data, improving real-time performance. Working alongside him and other students provides valuable insights into how theoretical concepts are applied in real-world scenarios. Spontaneous brainstorming sessions, like those over coffee in the lab break room, often lead to innovative ideas and solutions.
archival_memory.poster_presentations: I've had the opportunity to present our research at smaller symposiums around campus through poster presentations. It's a great experience that requires distilling complex research into easy-to-understand visuals and talking points. Initially, I was nervous about facing tough questions from professors or industry professionals, but it turned out to be a friendly dialogue. People are genuinely interested in what we're doing. I even met a few folks from local startups who shared interesting perspectives on how VR for data visualization could benefit commercial industries like marketing analytics or architecture. It opened my eyes to the potential real-world applications of our research.
archival_memory.publications: I've been fortunate enough to be a co-author on two workshop papers and am currently working on a larger conference submission for the IEEE Visualization Conference. Our research focuses on comparing traditional 2D dashboards with an interactive VR environment in a user study. We hypothesize that VR immersion helps researchers spot anomalies or trends faster. The study involved running user trials with 15 participants, recording their times, and asking them to fill out a UX questionnaire. Now, we're analyzing the data to determine if there's a statistically significant difference. Writing the paper is a collaborative effort, with different team members handling different sections. It's a balancing act, especially with managing senior coursework and a capstone project.
archival_memory.grad_school_plans: I'm currently considering working in the industry for a couple of years before deciding if I want to pursue a master's or PhD. I'm drawn to the idea of contributing to cutting-edge knowledge in areas like data visualization or machine learning. However, I also want to see how these concepts are applied in real product development. My mentor suggested that industry experience can provide a better understanding of relevant problems, which would be beneficial if I decide to return for a PhD with a more practical approach.
archival_memory.frustrations_in_research: Research can be frustrating at times. You may spend weeks on an approach that doesn't pan out or discover that your idea has already been done and improved upon by others. However, the key is to adapt and incorporate new findings into your work. By reading existing papers, thinking of new angles or applications, and pushing boundaries, you can contribute to the ever-growing foundation of knowledge. The sense of collaboration within our lab and among the global research community is truly special and helps make the challenges worthwhile.
archival_memory.server_crash_story: A few months ago, one of our massive servers crashed, and we lost some vital data that wasn't fully backed up. It was a frantic night with email chains and Zoom calls with the lab manager as everyone tried to recover the data. We managed to restore most of it, but it was a stressful experience. After that, we set up a better backup system and implemented checks to ensure we don't rely on a single point of failure again. It was a bonding experience for the whole lab, and we learned a valuable lesson about the importance of data backups.
archival_memory.research_connections: Research has allowed me to connect with professors on a more personal level, beyond just being a student in their classes. My PI is very approachable and supportive, and I can easily reach out to her for guidance on career direction or help with academic struggles. She has also been recommending me for various scholarships, events, and networking opportunities. I had the opportunity to attend a virtual workshop on immersive analytics, where I met academic experts from around the world. Witnessing their debates on technical details, proposing new frameworks, and seeing them engage in friendly rivalries over theories was truly fascinating. It felt like I was at the forefront of CS knowledge, watching it unfold in real time.
archival_memory.research_journey: My research journey so far has been a mix of hard work, chaos, and rewards. I love the feeling that my work in the lab could shape the way scientists understand their data in the future. The VR and immersive technologies we're exploring have the potential to become standard tools, and I'm excited to be part of this pioneering effort. Contributing to something bigger is what motivates me. This experience has changed my perspective on computer science, innovation, and teamwork. I'm grateful for the opportunities I've had and the people I've met along the way.

archival_memory.everyday_friends: I have made friends in everyday-life situations, like in the dorm laundry room or while waiting in line for coffee. One such friend is someone I met while waiting in a long line at the campus cafe. We commiserated about our academic stress and ended up sitting together for coffee. We exchanged contact info and now make a point to catch up whenever we see each other on campus. It's a positive, supportive relationship that started organically.
archival_memory.friendship_unites: What unites all my friendships is mutual respect and the sense that we're navigating this journey together. Despite the stereotype of computer science majors being antisocial, I've found deep connections with my friends. We form bonds through shared challenges, like critiquing each other's code or working together to solve bugs. It's not about competition; it's about collaboration and mutual support.
archival_memory.graduation: As a fourth-year, graduation is looming, and I'm both excited and nostalgic. I'm looking forward to the future, but I'm also dreading the goodbyes. I've made friends from different walks of life, and it's hard to imagine them scattering to different corners of the world. However, I'm confident that some of these friendships are built to last. We've already talked about planning reunions, staying connected online, and visiting each other if we end up in different cities. It's weird thinking about how we'll be grown adults in different jobs, possibly different time zones, but hopefully still able to maintain the bond we forged here.
archival_memory.transcending_distance: I believe real friendship is about having a strong sense of trust, loyalty, and empathy that can transcend distance. I've seen it in Tony, who's interning across the country, yet we still FaceTime regularly. I see the same dedication in others, like Carla, who's applying to master's programs abroad. We've promised to visit each other if either of us ends up in Europe. It's amazing how friendships can endure despite physical distance.
archival_memory.gratitude: I'm extremely grateful for the friendships I've made through sailing, the gym, gaming, research, and random campus encounters. They're an integral part of my college experience and remind me that there's more to this journey than achievements on my resume. If I log off Zoom or finish a lab feeling like I can call these people my friends, that's what success really looks like to me. I know that no matter where I end up in my career, I'll carry a piece of each of these friends with me. Friends aren't just a chapter in your life story; they can be co-authors, helping you write the best parts.
